permitsPage.title: Permit & Licensing Assistance
permitsPage.subtitle: Infrastructure Permits, Regulatory Coordination & Commercial Licensing Support
permitsPage.lead: We help project owners, ISPs, and contractors prepare permit documentation and coordinate with the relevant authorities and local stakeholders for infrastructure and commercial projects.
permitsPage.servicesDescription: Select the area that matches your project. Requirements differ by location, authority, and project type, so every engagement starts with a consultation.
permitsPage.card1: Assistance for road utilization permits, telecommunications infrastructure placement, and coordination with relevant road authorities.
permitsPage.card2: Support for aerial and underground fiber optic infrastructure, pole installation, and network deployment permissions.
permitsPage.card3: Assistance with excavation, duct installation, road crossing documentation, and restoration coordination.
permitsPage.card4: Coordination with village authorities, Banjar representatives, and local stakeholders for infrastructure projects.
permitsPage.card5: Assistance with land access agreements, infrastructure placement, lease coordination, and supporting documentation.
permitsPage.card6: Technical documentation and regulatory coordination for billboard and outdoor advertising installations.
permitsPage.card7: Assistance with route assessment, supporting documentation, and road-use dispensation for oversized or heavy cargo.
permitsPage.card8: Assistance and coordination for commercial content licensing and related usage permissions, including sports public viewing for venues.
permitsPage.noticeText: Jerco provides permit assistance and regulatory coordination. Permits and licenses are issued only by the competent authorities or, for commercial content, by the rights holders. Approval, requirements, fees, and processing times are determined by each issuer and may vary by location and project.
permitsPage.pvIntro: Showing live sports such as the Premier League, AFL, or NRL to guests in a bar, restaurant, hotel, villa, or beach club is a commercial public viewing. It requires a commercial license from the rights holder or its authorized distributor. Home or personal subscriptions do not cover commercial screening.
permitsPage.pvAvailability: Commercial rights, terms, and fees differ by competition, season, and territory, and are set by the rights holder.
permitsPage.pv1Text: List the competitions you want to show, venue type, capacity, and number of screens.
permitsPage.pv2Text: Find the rights holder or authorized distributor for commercial viewing of each competition in Indonesia.
permitsPage.pv3Text: Prepare venue data and supporting documents, and follow up the application with the licensor.
permitsPage.pv4Text: Set up receivers, IPTV, and TV distribution so licensed content reaches every screen in the venue.
permitsPage.pvDisclaimer: Jerco is not a broadcaster, rights holder, or official distributor, and is not affiliated with the leagues, organizers, or broadcasters mentioned. Competition names are trademarks of their respective owners.
permitsPage.processDescription: A structured workflow that keeps your documents, technical data, and coordination records organized from the first conversation onward.
permitsPage.step1Text: Discuss your project scope, location, and timeline to identify which permits may be relevant, based on the information you share.
permitsPage.step2Text: Help compile and organize supporting documents, drawings, route data, and technical attachments for the applicable process.
permitsPage.step3Text: Review technical data such as routes, KMZ/KML, drawings, and BOQ for completeness and consistency before submission.
permitsPage.step4Text: Support communication and coordination with the relevant authorities and local stakeholders throughout the process.
permitsPage.step5Text: Track progress, respond to requests for additional information, and keep records organized for your project files.
permitsPage.contactDescription: Share your project location, scope, and any existing drawings, route files (KMZ/KML), or documents. We will review them and discuss the next steps with you.

meta.description: How SI, VAR, Aggregator, and MSP differ for IT & telecom infrastructure projects. Choose the right contract type before work starts.

rolesPage.title: SI, VAR, Aggregator, and MSP — differences for infrastructure projects
rolesPage.lead: Four industry roles often get mixed because each “combines parties.” What differs: what is combined, and who owns the outcome. Pick the matching contract type — don’t buy boxes like a VAR and expect SI acceptance, or pay a monthly retainer and expect MSP monitoring.
rolesPage.ctaHelper: Split Implementation (SI) and Managed Service (MSP) line items before work starts.
rolesPage.defDescription: In short: what is combined, and how far responsibility goes.
rolesPage.defVar: Vendor product + value-add (setup, bundle, training, product support).
rolesPage.defAggregator: Many sources/channels combined into one access door.
rolesPage.defSi: Design, install, test, and hand over a multi-vendor system as one whole.
rolesPage.defMsp: Operate an already-accepted system, continuously, to an SLA.
rolesPage.reuse1: VAR finishes the product. SI finishes the system.
rolesPage.reuse2: An official vendor partner is not automatically an SI.
rolesPage.reuse3: An integrator makes systems work together. An aggregator gathers access/channels.
rolesPage.reuse4: “Already aggregated” is not the same as “already integrated.”
rolesPage.reuse5: SI builds until accepted. MSP operates what is already accepted.
rolesPage.reuse6: MSP does not start without handover: asset list, topology, credential procedure, backup status, known issue, vendor warranty, escalation SOP.
rolesPage.cmpDescription: Scroll horizontally on small screens, or read by aspect row.
rolesPage.cmpCaption: Comparison of VAR, Aggregator, SI, and MSP by contract aspect
rolesPage.cellFaseVar: Supply before or outside the build
rolesPage.cellGagalSi: Systems do not talk / failed acceptance
rolesPage.buyerDescription: One quick question before you pick a contract type.
rolesPage.buyer3If: Boxes power on but systems do not talk
rolesPage.buyer4If: Service is down — who responds in X minutes
rolesPage.seqDescription: An aggregator may sit beside the chain; it does not replace SI or MSP.
rolesPage.seq1Text: Business and technical needs are clarified.
rolesPage.seq3Text: Multi-vendor systems combined until ready to test.
rolesPage.seq5Text: Ongoing operations per agreed scope & SLA.
rolesPage.seqNote: Aggregator may sit beside chain; does not replace SI or MSP.

rolesPage.ex1Text: Powered boxes are not enough: Wi-Fi, CCTV, and PMS must talk — that is SI work before MSP keeps uptime.
rolesPage.ex2Text: Supply switch/AP (VAR if any) → SI design & test → acceptance → MSP operate if needed.
rolesPage.ex3Text: Build & documentation until accepted; post-handover operations are not supply-only work.
rolesPage.ctrDescription: One document may cover several roles — as long as scopes are not mixed.
rolesPage.ctrVar: SKU, qty, lead time, vendor warranty, per-item install services
rolesPage.ctrSi: requirement, topology, interface matrix, FAT/SAT, as-built, defects liability
rolesPage.ctrMsp: asset register, coverage window, severity, response/resolution, backup RPO/RTO if included, new-project exclusion
rolesPage.ctrAgg: catalog/channels, onboarding, settlement/routing — not site acceptance
rolesPage.jercoTitle: How Jerco positions SI & Managed Service
rolesPage.jercoSiText: Survey/design, install, integrate as specified, test, document, handover.
rolesPage.jercoMsText: Operate after acceptance per agreed scope.
rolesPage.jercoNoticeTitle: Not a marketplace & not a pure reseller
rolesPage.jercoNoticeText: This page does not position Jerco as a marketplace aggregator or pure product reseller. Product supply inside an SI project is not a VAR catalog business. There is no new service card named Aggregator.
rolesPage.cavTitle: Not a price list — and not empty labels
rolesPage.cav2: Monthly maintenance without SLA is not MSP.
rolesPage.faq1Q: What is the difference between SI and VAR?
rolesPage.faq1A: VAR finishes the product (SKU/license/bundle + value-add setup/training/product support). SI finishes the system: design, install, test, and hand over a multi-vendor system as one whole until accepted. An official vendor partner is not automatically an SI.
rolesPage.faq2Q: What is the difference between SI and MSP?
rolesPage.faq2A: SI builds until accepted (design→build→test→handover). MSP operates an already-accepted system, continuously, to an SLA. MSP does not start without handover: asset list, topology, credential procedure, backup status, known issue, vendor warranty, escalation SOP.
rolesPage.faq3Q: What is the difference between aggregator and integrator?
rolesPage.faq3A: An integrator (SI) makes systems work together. An aggregator gathers access/channels into one door. “Already aggregated” is not the same as “already integrated.” An aggregator does not replace SI or MSP.
rolesPage.faq4Q: When do you need SI and MSP?
rolesPage.faq4A: Typical sequence: Need → supply (VAR if needed) → SI design/build/test → acceptance + handover pack → MSP operate. Split Implementation (SI) and Managed Service (MSP) line items before work starts. Monthly maintenance without SLA is not MSP; rack-and-stack is not SI.
